HEMOCARE: Offline Blood Bank Management System
Standard Operating Procedures (SOP) • Safe Blood — Healthier Tomorrow

1. System Architecture & Offline Operation

HEMOCARE is a 100% self-contained, offline-first Blood Bank Management System designed for hospital transfusion services, regional blood distribution centers, and mobile blood drives. It requires no active internet connection, no external CDNs, and stores all operational records in an embedded SQLite database (bloodbank.db).

Standard Blood Banking Lifecycle

1. Donor Master → 2. Blood Donation → 3. Serology Screening → 4. Component Inventory → 5. Hospital Issue
Discard Path: Any unit found to have Reactive serology, damaged containers, or exceeded shelf life moves directly to Discard / Wastage.

2. User Authentication

Access to HEMOCARE is strictly authenticated through server-side hashed credentials and secure sessions.

  • Default administrative credentials: Username: admin | Password: admin123
  • Always click Sign Out from the sidebar when leaving the blood bank workstation.

3. Donor Master

Register voluntary or replacement blood donors with demographics, contact information, and blood group verification.

  • Unique Donor IDs (e.g. DNR0001) are generated automatically.
  • Accepted ABO/Rh Blood Groups: A+, A-, B+, B-, AB+, AB-, O+, O-.
  • Eligible donor age is standardly between 18 and 65 years. Donors marked as Deferred are temporarily restricted from blood collection.

4. Recording Blood Donation

When a donor arrives for phlebotomy:

  • Select the donor from the dropdown. The system automatically fetches Donor Name, verified Blood Group, and Age.
  • Enter collection volume (typically 450 mL or 350 mL) and unique collection bag barcode.
  • Select initial component type to register into inventory (Whole Blood, PRBC, FFP, or Platelets). Initial status is set to Pending Serology.

5. Serology Screening (TTI Testing)

Every collected blood unit must undergo mandatory testing for Transfusion-Transmissible Infections:

  • Mandatory 5-Panel Tests: HIV 1&2, HBsAg (Hepatitis B), HCV (Hepatitis C), Syphilis (VDRL), and Malaria.
  • Automated Calculation: If ANY test is Reactive, the overall screening result is automatically set to Reactive.
  • Strict Quarantine Rule: Reactive units are immediately quarantined and prohibited from issue. Only units with Non-Reactive across all 5 markers can be released for clinical use.

6. Supported Blood Components

HEMOCARE strictly manages and tracks exactly four therapeutic blood components:

Component Standard Shelf Life Recommended Storage
Whole Blood 35 Days +2°C to +6°C (Cold storage)
PRBC (Packed RBCs) 42 Days +2°C to +6°C
FFP (Fresh Frozen Plasma) 365 Days (1 Year) -20°C or colder
Platelets (RDP / Apheresis) 5 Days +20°C to +24°C (Agitator)

7. Issuing Blood to Hospitals

Issuance releases a verified, compatible blood unit to an authorized hospital or clinic:

  • The system strictly blocks issuance of: Reactive units, Expired units, already Issued units, and Discarded units.
  • Selecting a Unit ID automatically inspects and validates eligibility in real-time.
  • Upon confirmation, the unit lifecycle status changes to Issued and stock is automatically decremented.

8. Discard & Wastage Logging

Units that exceed expiry date, test reactive for infection, or suffer container breakage/leakage are documented in the Discard Register with the authorized officer's sign-off.

9. Dynamic Stock Matrix & Safety Alerts

Stock counts are never manually input. They are dynamically aggregated from all active inventory units where:
status = 'Available' AND serology_status = 'Non-Reactive' AND expiry_date >= Current Date.

If available units for any component fall below the safety threshold (default: 10 units), the system flags a LOW STOCK alert. Units reaching within 7 days of expiration are flagged as EXPIRING SOON.

10. Exporting Reports (Excel & PDF)

HEMOCARE generates 11 distinct operational reports with custom filters. Every report can be exported in two offline formats:

  • Excel (.xlsx): Formatted spreadsheets generated using openpyxl with auto-fitted column widths, freeze panes, and custom styling.
  • PDF (.pdf): Publication-ready medical reports generated using reportlab with headers, timestamps, and data tables.
